# AttributeSystem

`attribute`

The six character attributes (Strength, Vitality, Resistance, Agility, Intelligence, Perception), what each one feeds, and how skill use grows them. No classes and no levels: a character starts from creation and grows slowly from use. At base 10 in every attribute each derived stat equals the number the game used before attributes existed.

> Give each character a body that differs from another's through data that feeds existing systems, in keeping with KnowledgeIsProgression and NoPayToWin

## Attributes

| Field | Type | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| attributes | json | Attribute ids in display order; names and descriptions are catalog keys attr.<id>.name / attr.<id>.desc |
| base | integer | Starting value of every attribute; a save from before Phase 178 loads at this value |
| creationMin | integer | Lowest value character creation allows |
| creationMax | integer | Highest value character creation allows |
| hardCap | integer | No attribute grows above this value |
| derivation | json | Derived stats: { <stat>: { attribute, kind, base, perPoint, perPointBelow, min, max, unit? } }; stat = clamp(base + slope * (value - attribute base), min, max), slope = perPointBelow under the base, perPoint at or above it |
| growth | json | Growth from skill XP: { xpPerPoint, costStep, totalPointsCap, categories: { <skill category>: { <attribute>: weight } } }; the next point of an attribute that has grown g points costs xpPerPoint * (1 + costStep * g) weighted XP |

## Actions

### derive

Compute a character's derived stats from its attributes

**Conditions:**
- Each derived stat is fed by exactly one attribute through the derivation table; nothing else is hard-coded
- At base 10 in every attribute each derived stat equals today's constant (carry 40 kg, max HP 100, HP regeneration 0.25/s, every factor 1, every chance 0)
- The clamp keeps a 20-point gap noticeable but never a one-shot

### grow

Grow attributes from skill XP on the host

**Conditions:**
- XP granted in a skill category is split over that category's weighted attributes
- Each point grown makes the next point of that attribute cost more (diminishing returns)
- Growth stops at the hard cap per attribute and at totalPointsCap across all six
- Attributes never grow from spending points; the client sends no attribute values
